h: Huts, Bombes and a Station on the Doorstep
p: Some of the best moments are in the smallest rooms. Hut 8, where Alan Turing worked on the naval Enigma, has his office recreated, and Hut 6, which tackled army and air force messages, gives you a feel for the cramped, round-the-clock pressure the codebreakers worked under. Block B holds major exhibitions, and a working rebuild of a Bombe, the machine designed to speed up the hunt for Enigma settings, is a highlight when it's being demonstrated. Seeing the clattering drums whirring away makes the whole story click.

The Mansion is where it all began, and its odd mix of architectural styles is a talking point in itself. Out by the lake, take a moment to imagine the codebreakers on their breaks, sworn to secrecy and unable to tell even their families what they did.

Next door, the National Museum of Computing is a separate attraction with its own tickets, and it's where you'll find a working rebuild of Colossus along with plenty of vintage computers. Tech fans could easily spend a few extra hours there.

Getting here couldn't be easier by train, as Bletchley station is a short walk away, on the West Coast Main Line. Milton Keynes has plenty for the rest of the weekend: Willen Lake for watersports and lakeside walks, the famous concrete cows, and loads of shopping and indoor fun at Xscape and the centre:mk.
